---
name: experiment-preflight
description: Mandatory check before any results-bearing run (training, ablation, benchmark, evaluation sweep, pilot or calibration run) that the experiment measures what it claims. Builds a frozen packet, gets the reviews its tier requires (light: one fresh reviewer; full: fresh Claude + fresh Codex with blind reconstruction), and gates the start on them passing. Use before starting such a run, when writing a spec/prereg, when asked for a "preflight", or when reviewing an experiment packet.
---

# Experiment pre-flight

Implements the Experiments section of the global AGENTS.md. A repository procedure that
covers the same steps (e.g. a custody or prereg workflow) may replace the mechanics; it may
not drop a step without an explicit user decision. Invocation, exchange and recording of
reviews: skill `peer`.

## Roles
Author builds the packet. Coordinator dispatches reviewers and records verdicts. Full tier: two
reviewers, one fresh Claude session, one fresh Codex session. Light tier: one fresh reviewer.
The author is never a reviewer.

## Stages
- **Deterministic check with a known answer:** a test (asserted prediction, fails with the
  mechanism removed), not a packet.
- **Technical test** (it runs, shapes, no NaN, no crash; outputs not looked at as results):
  no pre-flight needed, results are not evidence.
- **Pilot / calibration packet:** anything whose outputs inform a decision, including smoke
  runs whose numbers are read, data statistics used for predictions, and instrument
  calibration. Reviewed prospectively: it states controls, expected signatures, budget and
  stop conditions, but need not supply the evidence it is meant to produce. Its results stay
  labelled as pilot exposure.
- **Confirmation packet:** requires the pilot's measurement checks to have passed. When the
  pilot only feeds thresholds that can be stated relatively (paired seeds, effect larger than a
  within-run repeat), pilot and confirmation are one packet and one review cycle.

## Tiers
- **Light:** no decision rests on the run, it is not a confirmation run, and it is either a
  short pilot or calibration (total budget over all cells and seeds within the limit the
  repository sets; without one, it is not short) or runs on synthetic data with a known ground
  truth. One file `packet.md`: the user's questions verbatim, gates with null probes, exact
  command, run plan, stop condition. One fresh reviewer, one round: alignment with the
  questions, what the command measures, applicable checklist items; then a delta answer on
  revisions. Commit the packet, then record outside it the commit hash and `sha256(packet.md)`:
  together they are the digest.
- **Full:** everything else, and whenever in doubt: both layers, manifest, two reviewers,
  procedure below.

## The packet (full tier)
Two layers, stored where the repository keeps specs/evidence (otherwise
`preflight/<run-id>/` next to the spec):

- **Layer A — intent-free** (`layer-a.md`): baseline and candidate commits with the diff,
  resolved config per cell, exact commands, run plan (cells, seeds, budget, stop conditions),
  data identifiers, paths of evaluation/metric code. No question, hypothesis or expectation.
- **Layer B — intent** (`layer-b.md`): opens with the user's questions verbatim (numbered)
  and, if the repository has a goal file, the goal item served and why this run is the shortest
  path to it; then question, hypothesis, prediction, what an ineffective
  method would show, kill condition, decision rule, controls, replication unit and size,
  smallest decision-relevant effect, analysis (metrics with units, summaries, selection rules).
- **Manifest** (`manifest.txt`): the content of everything the run reads, file by file, never
  through `git diff` (external diff and textconv drivers can change or empty its output). From
  the repository root:
  ```
  python3 <this skill>/manifest.py --exclude <packet dir> --exclude <run-output dirs or files> \
    <ignored inputs: data, configs, env files> <packet dir>/layer-a.md <packet dir>/layer-b.md \
    > <packet dir>/manifest.txt
  ```
  Tracked, submodule and untracked non-ignored files are included automatically, except under
  `--exclude`, which takes directories or files (so verdicts, logs, outputs of earlier cells and
  a status file updated at start do not change the digest).
  Untracked files inside submodules are not collected: pass any the run reads as extras. Record
  the exact manifest command in Layer A; the start gate reruns it unchanged. A large
  dataset may be passed as a file holding its immutable version id instead.
  Commit everything first, including the packet and any status file: the manifest records the
  commit, so a later commit changes the digest.
  **Packet digest = sha256 of `manifest.txt`.** Reviews and logs live outside the manifest. For
  the diff shown to reviewers use `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`.
  Self-check: `bash <this skill>/test_manifest.sh`.

## Reviewer procedure (full tier)
Round 1 gets Layer A plus repository access and states the rule: do not open specs, preregs or
result logs before round 2. (This is instruction-only; the reviewer could read them. Record it.)

1. **Reconstruct, from Layer A only:** what does each cell measure, in which units; what result
   would a no-op method produce; which degenerate solution would score well; what can this run
   not distinguish.
2. **Round 2 gets Layer B.** First judge whether the run serves the user's questions at all, and
   confirm or contradict the goal item and its shortest-path claim; then **compare** the
   reconstruction with the intent. Any mismatch is a blocker.
3. **Checklist** below plus every entry of the repository's LESSONS file: evidence, or `n/a`
   with a reason.
4. **Verdict:** `PASS | REVISE | BLOCK`, packet digest, reconstruction, mismatches, checklist
   results, blocking vs. optional findings.

## Checklist
Items marked † (5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 17, 19, 23) need evidence that a pilot or calibration run may be meant to produce. In a pilot
packet they are reviewed as a plan (what is measured, expected signature, stop condition); a
confirmation packet needs them passed.

**Question ↔ configuration**
1. The config is derived for this question; anything inherited from an earlier run is justified.
2. Every weight, threshold and tolerance has a unit and a reference scale checked against our
   data; numbers copied from papers or examples are converted; combined terms are compared in
   magnitude at initialization.
3. Borrowed terms are read from the implementation, not the paper: quantity, normalization,
   schedule, gradient paths, and whether an advertised feature actually fires.
4. If two scales or conditions coincide in all test cases, one case separates them.
5. † Predictions on new data follow a measurement of that data's own statistics.
6. Raw data and actual input/target examples were looked at, from the start and the end of each
   source.

**Mechanism** (each: if applicable)
7. † A deterministic check on a case with known answer shows the term does what the derivation
   says: values and gradients.
8. † Information flows, not only gradients: swapping or removing a source changes the output;
   changing hidden or future content leaves it unchanged.
9. † Teacher before student: an estimate used as a target beats the quantity it replaces.
10. The target is derivable from the input, and no shortcut lets the answer be read off an input.
11. Every path or case that should work is actually produced by the sampler.

**False successes**
12. Degenerate solutions (collapse, clones, shrink, wrong-but-consistent) are named and either
    excluded or caught by a hard gate. Collapse is measured scale-invariantly on the quantity
    that should carry information; no penalty can be bypassed by rescaling.
13. Ablations actually remove the information they claim to remove.
14. † A missing or deferred measurement is never a pass; it blocks.

**Measurement validity**
15. Metrics cannot be gamed: fixed units, coverage and signed values beside unsigned distances,
    subsets reported with counts, measured where targets differ rather than averaged away.
16. † Positive and negative controls show that the evaluation as a whole rejects the relevant
    false successes, not just that one mechanism works.
17. † Replication unit, justified number of replications, uncertainty analysis and the smallest
    decision-relevant effect are stated; the plan can separate that effect from noise.

**Comparison design**
18. Arms differ only in the variable under test: a switch does not shift random streams; equal
    seeds give equal weights, batches and evaluation data.
19. † Budgets are matched and long enough that the base task is learned in every arm.
20. Tuning and evaluation data are separate, and training cannot reach the evaluation set.
21. Selection rules (time point, aggregation, thresholds) are fixed before results are seen.
22. Randomized parameters are tested for their actual distribution, not only valid shapes.

**Execution**
23. † The real code path runs end to end with the final configuration (technical test, or a
    pilot packet if outputs are read).
24. Budget, guards and stop rules per stage, enforced in code; timeout means unevaluated, not
    failed; peak memory measured at the largest configuration.
25. Runtime or speed-up predictions follow a profile of the baseline and a cost model.
26. Shared devices: the repository's resource limits per device are respected; outputs are
    merged, never overwritten.

## Start gate
- Start only with the tier's `PASS` verdicts (light: one, full: two) on the same packet digest.
- Before **every** start, check the concrete cell against the run plan and the digest against
  the reviewed one. Light tier: the tree is clean at the recorded commit and `sha256(packet.md)`
  matches. Full tier: rebuild the manifest from the live state. Use the repository's runner if
  it does this, otherwise the coordinator does and records it.
- Any change outside the frozen run plan needs new reviews. No blanket approval for adaptive
  search.

## After the run
- Audit as a referee from raw outputs: recompute summaries, check units and controls.
- A changed analysis is a new, labelled exploratory version; the original analysis and raw data
  stay. Negative and failed runs are kept.
- An unexpected scientific outcome does not by itself stop or invalidate the remaining run plan.
  Document every surprise, its evidence and its effect on interpretation in the report, and
  continue the authorized plan. Enforced resource and technical validity limits still apply;
  any change to the plan or analysis must be explicit and versioned.
- Every avoidable loss becomes a lesson with its safeguard at the repository's canonical place.

     3	## User question (verbatim)
     4	1. "Dann bitte nyström Nutzung untersuchen und verbessern"
     5	
     6	Goal served: operator-directed continuation of METHOD-077. No standalone goal file applies.
     7	The shortest next step is to distinguish the first rejection from subsequent cached suppression,
     8	and test whether removing that suppression buys useful approximations or just repeated failures.
     9	The priority is unchanged accuracy and less total work, not an accepted-iteration count alone.
    10	This is a pilot, not a production-policy acceptance or a ranking of complete registrations.
    11	
    12	## Hypotheses and predictions for question 1
    13	- H1: sigma-only memory suppresses viable later approximations as source/weights/landmarks change.
    14	  Prediction: candidate accepts at least one later iteration for which baseline is suppressed.
    15	- H2: the fixed cost cap stops landmark growth before an acceptable approximation. Prediction:
    16	  attempted numerical/accuracy rejections followed by a logged cost stop.
    17	- H3: the narrow-kernel approximation remains invalid/inaccurate even when retried. Prediction:
    18	  additional candidate attempts but no additional accepted iterations; wall time can increase.
    19	An ineffective change shows no extra accepted iterations, or extra iterations without a clear
    20	end-to-end time reduction, or worse numerical outcomes. We do not interpret Nyström sparsity alone
    21	as a bug. First-failure diagnostics may expose a different next scope; no adaptive change is allowed.
    22	
    23	## Scope and limitations
    24	Seed 1, the `full` fixture and two representative sources (point/fixed and box/resampled), 20
    25	iterations, keep the cause of early fallback observable at bounded cost. They do not represent all
    26	nine variants, partial overlap, full convergence, or unseen shapes. The existing METHOD-077 Auto
    27	reference failed its truth gate; this pilot retains truth error and before/after visuals and cannot
    28	establish successful registration. Relative E-step equivalence to Auto is not proof of exact-dense
    29	identity. Normalization and solver parameters remain those of the existing experiment; this is not
    30	parameter tuning. Threads are 8 because this host has 8 physical cores (0-7), not the earlier host's
    31	16; absolute times cannot be compared with the old run. Both binaries have identical diagnostics.
    32	
    33	## Metrics, controls and predeclared verdict
    34	- Attempts, accepted iterations and cached suppressions: counts; attempt rejection classified as
    35	  numerical intermediate, sampled-error limit, cost cap, or cached suppression. Raw traces retained.
    36	- Native registration-call `seconds` includes preparation, all E/M work and diagnostic output, excluding
    37	  report generation. Two cold-start passes in reverse order expose order/noise; no population CI
    38	  or generalization claim from one seed. Candidate must beat the fastest baseline repeat by at
    39	  least 10% with its slowest repeat, in BOTH variants; otherwise do not adopt. This conservative
    40	  within-pilot screen can only justify a separately reviewed follow-up, never shipping.
    41	- RMS to current Auto reference <=1e-3, max <=1e-2 world units, same status/termination/iterations;
    42	  compared repeats must have identical deterministic outputs named in `assessed`.
    43	- Positive controls: Auto has zero Nystrom iterations; cost control has zero Nystrom iterations
    44	  and RMS to Auto <=2e-4 (existing METHOD-077 floor tolerance). Negative control must exceed
    45	  1e-3 RMS to Auto. Missing or failed controls make the comparison invalid, not passed.
    46	- Raw sampled-error limit .001, eigen cutoff 1e-10 and half-dense estimated-cost cap are unchanged.
    47	  Accuracy claims stay limited to the existing sampled check; neither the counter nor .001 is
    48	  a global entrywise bound. No threshold is inferred or tuned from this pilot.
    49	- `assessed` defines the frozen decision. Even if all screens pass, result is FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED.
    50	  Otherwise retain the negative finding and restore production selection. No larger run is
    51	  implicitly authorized by this packet, and no new variant is selected from it.
    52	
    53	## Measurement checks and technical validity
    54	Existing eight Nyström tests pass before edits. The added deterministic counterexample fails on
    55	baseline: after a separated-source rejection, a fresh evaluator accepts the new input while the
    56	reused evaluator suppresses it. The candidate passes all 29 Accelerated-suite tests. These tests
    57	are not evidence of a runtime gain in METHOD-077.
    58	The analysis self-check covers missing cells, a timing failure, a passing pilot screen and a
    59	parity failure, missing comparison values, and a timeout with partial trace output. Removing
    60	the timing rejection, stage parsing, or failure verdict makes the self-check fail. Numerical
    61	positive/negative controls of the pilot are reviewed prospectively, not assumed passed.
    62	Before freeze, technical-only calls of both binaries for both variants and the Auto reference
    63	use the final point count/threads/iteration cap and assert successful execution, finite trace
    64	values, and complete position buffers. Their efficacy and timing numbers are not inspected or
    65	used as results. Memory and wall limits are enforced for the evidence calls. The native code is
    66	CPU-only, no other builds or benchmark jobs are started during measurement.
    67	
    68	## Stop and reporting rules
    69	Manifest mismatch, missing approvals, process error, non-finite reported iteration state, missing
    70	position buffers, per-cell wall/address-space limit or total wall limit are technical stops; they
    71	cannot become a pass. A scientific negative result completes the remaining frozen cells.
    72	The driver generates HTML from raw output after each completed cell; it includes mechanism traces,
    73	stage boundaries, NLL and objective/prior curves and before/after views. BCPD has no additional
    74	weighted loss in its implemented stopping objective; full variational ELBO is not claimed.
    75	The original METHOD-077 evidence and its analysis are not changed. Any follow-up gets a new packet.

   133	
   134	A run is **results-bearing** when its outcome is used to support, refute, or set
   135	a claim, a parameter, or a decision: evidence-campaign runs, method
   136	reproductions and parity sessions, benchmark comparisons, `Operational` runs
   137	whose result enters a claim row, and the pilot, smoke, and calibration runs
   138	whose numbers inform any of these. A run that checks code against a pass/fail
   139	expectation fixed before the run, with no other use of its numbers, is
   140	verification (tests, a fix proof against a stated expected state).
   141	
   142	Every results-bearing run starts only after the global `experiment-preflight`
   143	skill (from the operator's agent-config repository): a frozen packet, two
   144	independent pre-run reviews (one fresh Claude and one fresh Codex session; the
   145	author is neither) with blind reconstruction, and a start check against the
   146	frozen run plan. This gate holds in every posture, including pair; the
   147	conversational pre-merge sweep does not replace it. Repository mapping:
   148	
   149	- Packet and verbatim verdicts live with the run's evidence:
   150	  `tasks/evidence/<ID>/preflight/<run>/` for task work, otherwise next to the
   151	  run's raw outputs (under `ara/evidence/` when a claim row will cite them). A
   152	  micro task's `evidence: not_applicable` exempts it from completion
   153	  artifacts, not from the pre-flight; no task file is created only to hold a
   154	  packet.
   155	- Pilot and calibration packets are reviewed prospectively; a confirmation run
   156	  needs the pilot's measurement checks passed (the skill's §Stages). Custody
   157	  profiles: [Experiment pre-flight under custody](workflow-evidence.md#experiment-pre-flight-under-custody).
   158	- Task and claim validators do not check packets or verdicts; the coordinator

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Deterministic manifest of everything a run reads; its sha256 is the packet digest.
     3	
     4	Usage (from the repository root):
     5	  manifest.py [--exclude PATH ...] [extra files or dirs ...] > DIR/manifest.txt
     6	Covers tracked files (with submodules) and untracked non-ignored files by content; symlinks by
     7	target and by the content behind them. Directories are walked, skipping `.git`, excluded
     8	directories, cycles, and links back to the repository root or its ancestors.
     9	Missing files appear as `missing`. Exclude (directory or file) the packet directory, run-output
    10	directories and files that change at start (e.g. a status file); pass
    11	ignored inputs (data, configs, env files) and layer-a.md / layer-b.md as extra paths. An extra
    12	inside an excluded directory is collected in full. Paths are used as given: rebuild the
    13	manifest with the identical command.
    14	Never uses git diff, so no diff or textconv driver can change the result.
    15	"""
    16	import hashlib
    17	import os
    18	import subprocess
    19	import sys
    20	
    21	
    22	def git(*args):
    23	    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    24	
    25	
    26	def inside(path, dirs):
    27	    return any(path == d or path.startswith(d.rstrip(os.sep) + os.sep) for d in dirs)
    28	
    29	
    30	def located(path):
    31	    """Absolute path with every component but the last resolved (a link stays a link)."""
    32	    return os.path.join(os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(path) or "."), os.path.basename(path))
    33	
    34	
    35	def entries(path, skip, ancestors=()):
    36	    real = os.path.realpath(path)
    37	    if ancestors and (os.path.basename(path) == ".git" or inside(real, skip)):
    38	        return
    39	    if os.path.islink(path):
    40	        yield f"link {os.readlink(path)}  {path}"
    41	    if os.path.isdir(real):
    42	        # ponytail: no visited set across names; a directory reachable under several names is
    43	        # hashed once per name. Fine unless links fan out heavily.
    44	        if real in ancestors or inside(root, [real]):
    45	            return
    46	        for name in sorted(os.listdir(real)):
    47	            yield from entries(os.path.join(path, name), skip, (*ancestors, real))
    48	    elif os.path.isfile(real):
    49	        h = hashlib.sha256()
    50	        with open(real, "rb") as f:
    51	            for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
    52	                h.update(block)
    53	        yield f"{h.hexdigest()}  {path}"
    54	    else:
    55	        yield f"missing  {path}"
    56	
    57	
    58	args, excluded_real = sys.argv[1:], []
    59	while args[:1] == ["--exclude"]:
    60	    excluded_real.append(os.path.realpath(args[1]))  # never abspath: it drops `..` lexically
    61	    args = args[2:]
    62	root = os.path.realpath(git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").strip())
    63	
    64	# Each top-level path maps to the directories its walk skips; an explicit extra inside an
    65	# excluded directory is still walked in full. Paths are used as given (rebuild with the same
    66	# command); walks share no state, so the result does not depend on argument order.
    67	listed = git("ls-files", "-z", "--recurse-submodules").split("\0")
    68	listed += git("ls-files", "-z", "--others", "--exclude-standard").split("\0")
    69	tops = {p: excluded_real for p in listed if p and not inside(located(p), excluded_real)}
    70	for extra in args:
    71	    tops[extra] = [d for d in excluded_real if not inside(os.path.realpath(extra), [d])]
    72	
    73	print("commit", git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip())
    74	print("\n".join(sorted({e for p, skip in tops.items() for e in entries(p, skip)})))
